definition: A method for aggregating multiple model outputs by selecting the answer that appears most frequently among several independently generated responses.
details: Majority voting, closely related to self-consistency, is a simple but effective way to improve accuracy on tasks with a single correct answer by leveraging agreement across multiple sampled reasoning attempts.

explainer.lead: Majority voting aggregates multiple model outputs by selecting the answer that appears most frequently among several independently generated responses. It is closely related to self-consistency and is a simple but effective way to improve accuracy on tasks with a single correct answer by leveraging agreement across sampled reasoning attempts.

tiers.eli5: Ask the same question several times and go with the answer most attempts agree on.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers sample several reasoning attempts and take the most frequent answer; a pitfall is that it only helps when there is a single correct answer to agree on.
tiers.paperLevel: Majority voting selects the most frequent answer among independently generated responses; it is closely related to self-consistency and relies on agreement across sampled reasoning attempts.

explainer.example: Five sampled reasoning attempts produce three '42' and two other answers, so '42' is selected.
